requirements.subject: ent:getreply-operation
requirements.canonical: The `getreply` operation IS used to handle replies from a previously called procedure.
requirements.original: The getreply operation is used to handle replies from a previously called procedure.

requirements.subject: ent:getreply-operation
requirements.canonical: The `getreply` operation has the syntax [`@nodefault`] (ObjectReference | `any port` | `any from` PortArrayRef) "." `getreply` ["(" TemplateInstance [`value` TemplateInstance] ")"] [`from` Address] ["->" [`value` (ValueRef | "(" {ValueRef [":=" [`@decoded` ["(" Expression ")"]] FieldOrTypeReference] [","]} ")")] [`param` "(" ({ValueRef ":=" [`@decoded` ["(" Expression ")"]] ParameterIdentifier ","} | {(ValueRef | "-") ","}) ")"] [`sender` ValueRef] [`@index` `value` ValueRef]].
requirements.original: [ @nodefault ] ( ObjectReference | any port | any from PortArrayRef ) "." getreply [ "(" TemplateInstance [ value TemplateInstance ]")" ] [ from Address ] [ "->" [ value ... ] [ param ... ] [ sender ValueRef] [ @index value ValueRef] ]

requirements.subject: ent:from-clause
requirements.canonical: The Address in the `from` clause of a `getreply` operation MAY be an AddressRef, a list of AddressRefs or `any component`.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: _Address may be an AddressRef, a list of AddressRef-s or "any component"._

requirements.subject: ent:getreply-operation
requirements.canonical: The `getreply` operation SHALL remove the top reply from the incoming port queue if, and only if, the matching criteria associated with the `getreply` operation are fulfilled.
requirements.original: The getreply operation shall remove the top reply from the incoming port queue, if, and only if, the matching criteria associated to the getreply operation are fulfilled.

requirements.subject: ent:matching-criteria
requirements.canonical: The matching criteria of a `getreply` operation ARE related to the signature of the procedure to be processed and to the communication partner.
requirements.original: These matching criteria are related to the signature of the procedure to be processed and the communication partner.

requirements.subject: ent:matching-criteria
requirements.canonical: The signature matching criteria of a `getreply` operation MAY be specified in-line or be derived from a signature template.
requirements.original: The matching criteria for the signature may either be specified in-line or be derived from a signature template.

requirements.subject: ent:value-keyword
requirements.canonical: Matching against a received return value in a `getreply` operation MAY be specified by using the `value` keyword.
requirements.original: Matching against a received return value can be specified by using the value keyword.

requirements.subject: ent:getreply-operation
requirements.canonical: In case of one-to-many connections, a `getreply` operation MAY be restricted to a certain communication partner.
requirements.original: A getreply operation may be restricted to a certain communication partner in case of one-to-many connections.

requirements.subject: ent:from-clause
requirements.canonical: A restriction of a `getreply` operation to a communication partner SHALL be denoted by the `from` keyword followed by an address or component reference, a list of address or component references, or `any component`.
requirements.original: This restriction shall be denoted by using the from keyword followed by a specification of an address or component reference, a list of address or component references or any component.

requirements.subject: ent:from-clause
requirements.canonical: For one-to-one connections, which are a simple case of one-to-many connections, the `from` clause MAY be used in a `getreply` operation.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: The one-to-one connection is considered to be a simple case of the one-to-many connections and allows the usage of the from-clause.

requirements.subject: ent:assignment-part
requirements.canonical: The assignment of out and inout parameter values to variables SHALL be made in the assignment part of the `getreply` operation.
requirements.original: The assignment of out and inout parameter values to variables shall be made in the assignment part of the getreply operation.

requirements.subject: ent:signature-template
requirements.canonical: Making out and inout parameter assignments in the assignment part ALLOWS signature templates to be used in `getreply` operations in the same manner as templates are used for types.
requirements.original: This allows the use of signature templates in getreply operations in the same manner as templates are used for types.

requirements.subject: ent:assignment-part
requirements.canonical: The optional assignment part of the `getreply` operation IS composed of the assignment of out and inout parameter values to variables and the retrieval of the address of the sender of the reply.
requirements.original: The (optional) assignment part of the getreply operation comprises the assignment of out and inout parameter values to variables and the retrieval of the address of the sender of the reply.

requirements.subject: ent:value-keyword
requirements.canonical: The `value` keyword in the assignment part of a `getreply` operation IS used to retrieve the return value of a reply.
requirements.original: The keyword value is used to retrieve return values and the keyword param is used to retrieve the parameter values of a reply.

requirements.subject: ent:param-keyword
requirements.canonical: The `param` keyword in the assignment part of a `getreply` operation IS used to retrieve the parameter values of a reply.
requirements.original: The keyword value is used to retrieve return values and the keyword param is used to retrieve the parameter values of a reply.

requirements.subject: ent:sender-keyword
requirements.canonical: The `sender` keyword in the assignment part of a `getreply` operation IS used to retrieve the address of the sender of the reply.
requirements.original: The keyword sender is used when it is required to retrieve the address of the sender.

requirements.subject: ent:decoded-modifier
requirements.canonical: When individual parameters or referenced fields of the return value of a reply are assigned, encoded parameters MAY be decoded prior to assignment by using the `@decoded` modifier.
requirements.original: When assigning individual parameters or referenced fields of the return value of a reply, encoded parameters can be decoded prior to assignment using the @decoded modifier.

requirements.subject: ent:decoded-modifier
requirements.canonical: If the `@decoded` modifier is used, the referenced parameter or field of the return value on the right hand side of the assignment SHALL be of a bitstring, hexstring, octetstring, charstring or universal charstring type.
requirements.original: In this case, the referenced parameter or field of the return value on the right hand sided of the assignment shall be one of the bitstring, hexstring, octetstring, charstring or universal charstring types.

requirements.subject: ent:decoded-modifier
requirements.canonical: If the `@decoded` modifier is used, the referenced parameter or field SHALL be decoded into a value of the same type as the variable on the left hand side of the assignment.
requirements.original: It shall be decoded into a value of the same type as the variable on the left hand side of the assignment.

requirements.subject: ent:decoded-modifier
requirements.canonical: A failure of the decoding of a parameter or field with the `@decoded` modifier in a `getreply` operation SHALL cause a test case error.
requirements.original: Failure of this decoding shall cause a test case error.

requirements.subject: ent:decoded-modifier
requirements.condition: the parameter or field is of universal charstring type
requirements.canonical: If the parameter or referenced field of the return value is of the universal charstring type, the `@decoded` clause MAY contain an optional parameter defining the encoding format.
requirements.original: In case the parameter or referenced field of the return value is of the universal `charstring type, the @decoded clause can contain an` optional parameter defining the encoding format.

requirements.subject: ent:decoded-modifier
requirements.canonical: The encoding format parameter of the `@decoded` clause SHALL be of the charstring type.
requirements.original: The parameter shall be of the charstring type and it shall contain one of the strings allowed for the decvalue_unichar function (specified in clause C.5.4).

requirements.subject: ent:decoded-modifier
requirements.canonical: The encoding format parameter of the `@decoded` clause SHALL contain one of the strings allowed for the `decvalue_unichar` function.
requirements.original: The parameter shall be of the charstring type and it shall contain one of the strings allowed for the decvalue_unichar function (specified in clause C.5.4).

requirements.subject: ent:decoded-modifier
requirements.canonical: An encoding format parameter value of the `@decoded` clause other than the strings allowed for `decvalue_unichar` SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: Any other value shall cause an error.

readings: An invalid encoding format parameter value of the `@decoded` clause SHALL cause a test case error at runtime.
An invalid encoding format parameter value of the `@decoded` clause SHALL cause a compile-time error when it is statically known.
ambiguity.issue: The kind of error (compile-time or test case error) is not stated; the canonical keeps the generic 'error'.

requirements.subject: ent:decoded-modifier
requirements.condition: the parameter or field is not of universal charstring type
requirements.canonical: If the parameter or referenced field of the return value is not of the universal charstring type, the optional encoding format parameter of the `@decoded` clause SHALL NOT be present.
requirements.original: In case the parameter or referenced field of the return value is not a universal **char string, the** optional parameter shall not be present.

ambiguity.issue: The text writes 'universal char string' (PDF formatting artefact) where the type 'universal charstring' is meant.

requirements.subject: ent:get-any-reply
requirements.canonical: A `getreply` operation with no argument list for the signature matching criteria SHALL remove the reply on the top of the incoming port queue, if any, if all other matching criteria are fulfilled.
requirements.original: A getreply operation with no argument list for the signature matching criteria shall remove the reply message on the top of the incoming port queue (if any) if all other matching criteria are fulfilled.

requirements.subject: ent:get-any-reply
requirements.condition: used in the response and exception handling part of a call operation
requirements.canonical: If a get any reply operation is used in the response and exception handling part of a `call` operation, it SHALL only treat replies from the procedure invoked by that `call` operation.
requirements.original: If GetAnyReply is used in the response and exception handling part of a call operation, it shall only treat replies from the procedure invoked by the call operation.

improper_terms.proper: get any reply (getreply operation without signature argument)

ambiguity.issue: 'GetAnyReply' is a BNF-style name that is not defined in this clause; the 'get any reply' form of the getreply operation is meant.

requirements.subject: ent:any-port
requirements.canonical: A `getreply` operation on any port IS specified by using the `any port` keywords.
requirements.original: To get a reply on any port, use the any port keywords.

requirements.subject: ent:any-from-port-array
requirements.canonical: A `getreply` operation on any port of a specific port array IS specified by using the `any from` PortArrayRef syntax.
requirements.original: To get a reply on any port from a specific port array, use the any from PortArrayRef syntax where PortArrayRef shall be a reference to a port array identifier.

requirements.subject: ent:any-from-port-array
requirements.canonical: The PortArrayRef in an `any from` PortArrayRef construct of a `getreply` operation SHALL be a reference to a port array identifier.
requirements.original: To get a reply on any port from a specific port array, use the any from PortArrayRef syntax where PortArrayRef shall be a reference to a port array identifier.

requirements.subject: ent:index-redirection
requirements.canonical: The index of the port of a single-dimensional port array at which the `getreply` operation was successful MAY be stored in a variable of type integer.
requirements.original: It is also possible to store the index of a port in a single-dimensional port array at which the operation was successful to a variable of type integer or, in case of multi-dimensional port arrays the index of the successful port to an integer array or record of integer variable.

requirements.subject: ent:index-redirection
requirements.canonical: For a multi-dimensional port array, the index of the port at which the `getreply` operation was successful MAY be stored in an integer array or record of integer variable.
requirements.original: It is also possible to store the index of a port in a single-dimensional port array at which the operation was successful to a variable of type integer or, in case of multi-dimensional port arrays the index of the successful port to an integer array or record of integer variable.

requirements.subject: ent:any-from-port-array
requirements.canonical: When a port array is checked for matching replies, the port indices to be checked ARE iterated from lowest to highest.
requirements.original: When checking the port array for matching replies, the port indices to be checked are iterated from lowest to highest.

requirements.subject: ent:any-from-port-array
requirements.canonical: If the port array is multi-dimensional, the ports ARE iterated over from the innermost to the outermost array dimension, from lowest to highest index for each dimension (e.g. [0][0], [0][1], [1][0], [1][1]).
requirements.original: If the port array is multi-dimensional, then the ports are iterated over from innermost to outermost array dimension from lowest to highest index for each dimension, e.g. [0][0], [0][1], [1][0], [1][1].

readings: The last index varies fastest, as shown by the example sequence [0][0], [0][1], [1][0], [1][1].
The innermost dimension (first index) is iterated over first, i.e. the first index varies fastest.
ambiguity.issue: 'From innermost to outermost' could be read as the first index varying fastest, but the example sequence shows the last index varying fastest; the canonical follows the example.

requirements.subject: ent:any-from-port-array
requirements.canonical: The first port of the port array that matches all the criteria CAUSES the `getreply` operation to be successful, even if other ports in the array would also meet the criteria.
requirements.original: The first port which matches all the criteria will cause the operation to be successful even if other ports in the array would also meet the criteria.

non_requirement.reason: paragraph heading 'Get a reply on any port'
paragraph heading 'Get a reply on any port from a port array'
